notes: Added after the first results because all-or-nothing over about 187 questions saturates at 0 for every lane. One deterministic OK-versus-dispute rule, no tuned threshold. Scored from recorded answers on the frozen 100. No new model call.

Gold disputed amount is max(0, printed patient responsibility - correct patient responsibility) on a gold-dispute line. Caught dollars are that amount where the model verdict is also dispute. False-alarm dollars are the printed patient responsibility where the model disputes a gold-OK line. No threshold.
Primary rows are the frozen 100 (ladder_hard_ids.json) except DeepSeek, whose run file stopped early and is marked partial.

The OK-versus-dispute files were added after the first results. line_all_checks is the earlier all-six line score from hard_test_*_line_verdict.json on the same 100, where that file exists. Cheaper models have no recorded all-six file, so that metric is empty. strict_case stays beside both. The 300-case question-accuracy slice is a different denominator.
Drex $/1,000 is the stored Drex token cost in ladder_summary.json ($0.03 per million input tokens). It is not a fresh Nace invoice.
Latency is the median of recorded per-case latency_ms on the cited run. Drex answer logs repeat that call latency on each question; one copy is kept.

Where ladder_summary.json has a list $/1,000 for that model, that recorded figure is used. Hybrid and the BillProof system use the mean of recorded list_cost_usd, or cost_usd when list_cost_usd is absent.

Qwen and DeepSeek lanes are recorded DeepInfra answers on the longest prefix of the frozen order where Drex also has an answer. drex_then_* keeps Drex when recorded confidence is at least 0.90 and otherwise uses that model's recorded answer. t=0.90 was not tuned: these rows are the reported set, and no DeepInfra run exists on a separate dev or practice split. partial means the prefix is short of the frozen n. Combo $/1,000 is Drex's recorded cost plus the recorded DeepInfra cost scaled to the routed share of the packed call.

benchmarks.metric_definition: Hard points are question accuracy. Prior-auth points are whole-case accuracy. Costs are list price from tokens, as stored in ladder_summary.json.

notes: This is the ladder's own metric. The hard benchmark's primary number is the OK-versus-dispute line verdict, not this question accuracy.
DeepSeek is a prefix of the frozen order, marked partial. It is not a sample chosen by score.

Cheaper models use ladder_hard_*_question_accuracy.json. GPT-6.1 Sol, Drex v1.1, and Drex finance use hard_outcome_*_question_accuracy.json on the same 100 cases. Their p50 latency is the per-case median from the hard answer files.
If a point has no question-level file, k and the Wilson interval stay empty. ladder_summary n is a case count and is not used to recover k.

benchmarks.title: Command Center queue
benchmarks.tests: Replay of the prior-auth queue: Drex decides every request; GPT is a measured sample scaled to the queue for time and cost.
benchmarks.metric_definition: Share of queue decisions matching gold. GPT accuracy is the measured sample only and is not projected.

extra.note: Time and cost scale the measured per-case mean to the full queue. GPT latency includes shared router rate-limit wait. Accuracy is the measured sample only; it is not projected.

notes: GPT time and cost on the full queue are projected from the measured sample. The projection is labelled.
GPT $/1,000 uses cc_gpt_projected_cost_per_1000_list.json when that file exists.
Drex latency is the median of recorded queue_replay.jsonl latency_ms when that field is present.

benchmarks.title: Command Center rule change
benchmarks.tests: What flips if every published OR list is tightened to AND, using the same recorded Drex facts.
benchmarks.metric_definition: Share of affected requests whose decision changes when the combining rule changes. k is the flip count. Not an accuracy.

benchmarks.title: Command Center what-decides
benchmarks.tests: Does the record Drex names as deciding match the gold deciding record?

notes: Not a simulated run. Cost is total_cost_usd divided by n_scored, times 1000.

benchmarks.title: Full-chain demo
benchmarks.tests: Five scripted prior-auth packets: public policy page, NDI boxes, search, Drex, letter.
benchmarks.metric_definition: Share of the five evidence files whose top-level decision equals gold_decision.
notes: Five hand-built demo packets, not a random sample. The Wilson interval is wide because n=5.
The table shows the five-case recorded total, not a scaled $/1,000. Scaling five demo packets would read as about $100 per thousand.
Drex latency is timings.drex_ms only. Browser, NDI, and search seconds are in the same timings object and are not folded into this median.
